title: Provider capability record
description: Fail-closed record of a provider CLI's interrupt/resume behavior at a specific version. Every boolean defaults to false and may be set true only by a passing live probe. Adapters may claim mid-flight interrupt steering only when the matching flags are true; otherwise they must fall back to checkpoint-at-completion steering plus a fresh-session recovery packet.

cli_version.description: Exact CLI version string captured at probe time (e.g. '2.1.251').

model.description: Model used for the probe, or null when the CLI default was used.

probed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the probe run completed.

probe_tool_version.description: Version of the Papaya Agent Runtime probe harness that produced this record.

capabilities.description: Derived booleans. Absent proof means false (fail-closed).

session_id_in_stream.description: A durable session/thread id is emitted in the structured event stream.

usage_in_stream.description: Token/usage accounting appears in the structured event stream.

resume_after_clean_exit.description: A session that completed cleanly can be resumed by its id in a new process.

session_survives_process_exit.description: The session transcript persists on disk after the process exits.

resume_after_sigint_model_turn.description: A session interrupted with SIGINT during a model turn (before any tool) is resumable by id.

resume_after_sigint_tool.description: A session interrupted with SIGINT during a long tool command is resumable by id.

resume_after_sigkill.description: A session whose process group was SIGKILLed is still resumable by id.

worktree_resume.description: A session started in one checkout can be resumed by id from a linked git worktree.

duplicate_resume_ok.description: Resuming the same session id twice succeeds both times (idempotent late/duplicate delivery).

mid_process_steer.description: The provider accepts a follow-up/steer message into the same running process without exit.

requires_resume_prompt.description: Resume requires a non-empty prompt or stdin; there is no promptless follow mode.

orphan_tool_process.description: A tool child process survives a process-group SIGINT (orphaned work that recovery must reconcile).

scenarios.description: Per-scenario evidence used to derive the capabilities.
